guideRule.value: Required on paper since 1 April 2023; not applied in Khumbu, and unevenly enforced in Annapurna and Langtang
guideRule.detail: The Nepal Tourism Board's revised TIMS provision, effective 31 March 2023, says foreign trekkers on its listed national-park and conservation-area routes (Everest, Annapurna, Langtang and Manaslu among them) must walk with a licensed guide and carry a TIMS card issued by a registered agency. Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality rejected the rule and still registers independent trekkers at Lukla; in Annapurna and Langtang the rule stands, but 2025–26 reports conflict, with agencies saying guide licences are checked and independent accounts saying TIMS checkposts are mostly unstaffed, while restricted areas always require a guide and an agency.

guideDailyRate.value: About USD 25–40 a day (roughly NPR 3,800–6,100); a few agencies quote up to USD 50
guideDailyRate.detail: These are 2026 agency prices for a licensed, English-speaking trekking guide. Most quotes are USD 25–30, rising to USD 35–40 or more for senior guides, harder routes and restricted areas. As a floor, the trekking agencies' association set a minimum guide wage of NPR 3,100 a day from 17 July 2023; we found no later revision. The price normally covers the guide's own food, lodging and insurance, but agencies word this differently, so ask. Ask too whether their transport, such as a Lukla flight, is included. Your tip is extra.

porterDailyRate.value: About USD 18–25 a day (roughly NPR 2,700–3,800); some agencies quote up to USD 30
porterDailyRate.detail: These are 2026 agency prices for a porter who carries 20–25 kg, usually the bags of two trekkers. As a floor, the trekking agencies' association set a minimum porter wage of NPR 2,400 a day from 17 July 2023; we found no later revision. The price normally covers the porter's own food and lodging, but agencies differ, so ask what is included and ask to see the insurance. Your tip is extra.

porterGuideDailyRate.value: About USD 20–35 a day (roughly NPR 3,000–5,300), between a porter's rate and a guide's
porterGuideDailyRate.detail: A porter-guide carries a lighter load than a porter and guides in basic English. We found only two 2026 price sources and they differ: one gives USD 20–28 and the other USD 25–35. The trekking agencies' association treats porter-guide as its own wage grade, with a minimum of NPR 2,500 a day from 17 July 2023, and runs porter-guide training. We found no separate government licence for the role, so if your route requires a licensed guide, ask whether yours holds a trekking guide licence.

porterLoadLimit.value: 30 kg is the International Porter Protection Group's ceiling for Nepal; agencies normally load 20–25 kg, usually the bags of two trekkers
porterLoadLimit.detail: The International Porter Protection Group says no porter should carry more than they safely can, with 30 kg as the most in Nepal, and that the limit should come down for altitude, trail and weather. Agencies in 2026 describe 20–25 kg a porter, which is why two trekkers sharing one are asked to keep their bags to about 10–12 kg each. We found no current Nepali rule that fixes a load for trekking porters, and the trekking agencies' association's published wage agreements do not mention one. The guideline, as the bodies we checked quote it, does not say whether the porter's own kit counts, so assume it does and pack lighter.

porterWelfare.value: Five IPPG guidelines: proper clothing, shelter and food, insurance and equal medical care, no sick porter sent down alone, and a load within the porter's ability
porterWelfare.detail: The International Porter Protection Group asks that porters get clothing and footwear fit for the season and altitude, adequate shelter, food and drink, and life insurance with the same medical care you would expect yourself. A sick or injured porter must not be paid off and sent down alone: the trek leader has to be told, and someone who speaks the porter's language goes down with them. Nobody should carry more than they safely can, 30 kg at most in Nepal. Nepal's own rules for trekking agencies, as amended in 2018, also require the staff who go with you to have accident insurance of at least NPR 1,000,000 for the whole trip, so ask the agency to show you the policy.

teahouseDailyCost.value: Roughly USD 25–50 a day for a bed and three meals in Annapurna and Langtang and USD 35–65 in the Everest region; we found no reliable separate figure for Manaslu
teahouseDailyCost.detail: These are 2026 agency estimates and they vary a lot. One puts Langtang at USD 30–45, the lower Annapurna treks at USD 25–40, Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal at USD 30–50 and Everest at USD 35–65. A general guide says USD 25–55 depending on altitude and season. The room is the cheap part, often USD 2–10 a night, and some lodges discount it if you eat all your meals there. Prices climb with altitude, and hot showers, charging, Wi-Fi, boiled water, snacks and alcohol cost extra. For the Manaslu circuit, budget towards the top of the range.

gearRental.value: About USD 1–2 (NPR 150–300) per item per day for a down jacket or a sleeping bag in Thamel and at Lakeside in Pokhara; trekking poles cost less
gearRental.detail: Two 2026 guides give about USD 1–2 a day for a down jacket or a sleeping bag, USD 0.50–1 for a pair of trekking poles and about USD 1, or NPR 200–300, for microspikes or crampons. A third quotes far more, USD 5–15 a day for a jacket or bag, so prices clearly vary with the shop and the quality. You pay for every day the gear is out, and shops hold a cash deposit, put at USD 50–200 by the one guide that gives a figure. We found no shop price list to confirm any of this. Check zips, seams and warmth before you leave the shop, because copies of well-known brands are common in Thamel.

helicopterRescueCost.value: About USD 3,000–6,000 from the upper Khumbu, USD 2,500–4,000 from Annapurna Base Camp to Pokhara and USD 2,500–5,500 from Langtang to Kathmandu; insure for helicopter evacuation up to 6,000 m
helicopterRescueCost.detail: These are operator and agency estimates for 2025–26 and differ about twofold for the same pick-up, with some quotes for Gorak Shep or Everest Base Camp reaching USD 8,000–12,000; the UK government puts the price at GBP 1,000–2,000 or more per flying hour. Check that your policy names helicopter evacuation and covers trekking to your highest point (5,545 m on Kala Patthar, 5,416 m on the Thorong La), because many standard and credit-card policies stop at 3,000 m or lower.

touristVisa.value: USD 30 for 15 days, USD 50 for 30 days, USD 125 for 90 days
touristVisa.detail: The Nepal Tourism Board lists these fees for a multiple-entry tourist visa. They are paid in US dollars or another convertible currency; the board says cards are accepted too, but carry cash in case the machines are down. Visas are issued on arrival at the Kathmandu, Pokhara and Gautam Buddha (Lumbini) international airports and at the land border posts. An extension costs USD 45 for the first 15 days and USD 3 a day after that, at the immigration offices in Kathmandu and Pokhara. Indian citizens do not need a visa, children under 10 get one free (US citizens excepted), and citizens of a short list of countries must get a visa before they travel. An online e-visa with card payment was due to go fully live on 17 August 2026. We could not open the Department of Immigration's own pages to see how it works now, so check before you fly.

luklaFlights.value: From Manthali (Ramechhap) in peak season, roughly April–May and October–November, and from Kathmandu otherwise; in 2026 agents quote foreigners about USD 180–230 one way from Manthali and USD 235–290 from Kathmandu
luklaFlights.detail: In autumn 2026 the flights again ran from Manthali, with extra flights from 29 September. The switch is made each peak season to ease congestion at Kathmandu airport, and the dates move from year to year. Manthali is a four to five hour drive from Kathmandu, and transfers for the early flights leave in the middle of the night. Airlines raised fares on 1 March 2026, and domestic airfares rose again in April when fuel costs spiked. The fares above come from booking agents, not the airlines: for Manthali one lists USD 198 and another USD 180–230, and for Kathmandu two agree on about USD 237. We could not check the Civil Aviation Authority's notices, so confirm the airport, the dates and the fare with the airline or your agency before you book anything else. Fare pages disagree after these changes: those quoting the airline fare list in force since August 2026 give about USD 254 from Kathmandu and USD 209 from Manthali.

mobileCoverage.value: Carry a Nepal Telecom (NTC) SIM, an Ncell SIM or both: 2026 guides favour NTC in Annapurna and disagree about the Everest trail, and high up paid lodge Wi-Fi often works when neither SIM does
mobileCoverage.detail: Most 2026 guides favour NTC on the Annapurna Circuit and for wider coverage on remote routes; they describe its signal as patchy above Manang and on the Thorong La. For the Everest trail they split, some saying Ncell is faster with good signal and others that NTC reaches further. In Khumbu the paid Everest Link Wi-Fi service runs as far as Gorak Shep, slowly. We found little route-by-route information for Langtang and Manaslu, where one guide prefers NTC, and we did not check either operator's coverage map. Expect long stretches with no signal on any high or remote route, and tell people at home before you go quiet.

drinkingWater.value: Treat all water yourself or buy boiled or filtered refills, and carry a refillable bottle: plastic bottles are banned on the Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal trails, and bottled soft drinks in Khumbu
drinkingWater.detail: Tap and stream water is not safe untreated anywhere on the trails, so use a filter, purification tablets or a UV pen, or pay a lodge for boiled water. The Annapurna conservation project's waste rules, as reported by the national news agency, ban carrying plastic and glass bottles to Annapurna Base Camp, Mardi Himal and Tara Hill Top. Travel guides say the ban is loosely enforced, and that safe drinking water stations and most lodges refill bottles along the Annapurna trails. Khumbu's municipality banned thin single-use plastic and drinks in plastic bottles from January 2020; reports at the time said bottled water was left out. We found no official 2025–26 statement on either rule, and no current list of refill stations or prices.

agencyLicensing.value: A registered company with a Department of Tourism trekking licence, PAN/VAT registration and a Nepal Rastra Bank licence to handle foreign currency; you can look it up in TAAN's member list
agencyLicensing.detail: TAAN, the trekking agencies' association, asks a company for these papers before it can join: its company registration, the Department of Tourism's licence to run a trekking business, a PAN/VAT certificate and Nepal Rastra Bank's foreign exchange licence. Ask the agency for the numbers and look it up in TAAN's general members list, which showed 2,344 agencies on 22 November 2026. Nepal Rastra Bank also publishes the businesses it has licensed for foreign exchange. Only a registered agency can buy a TIMS card or apply for a restricted-area permit, so a company that cannot show its papers cannot legally arrange either.

guideLicensing.value: Guides qualify through a five-week trekking guide course at the Nepal Academy of Tourism and Hotel Management (NATHM) and carry a licence that has to be renewed
guideLicensing.detail: NATHM's 2026 notices describe a five-week trekking guide course with 300–500 places, open to applicants who have passed class 12, or class 10 with two years at a registered trekking agency. A 2012 agreement between the trekking agencies' association and the workers' unions shows that the licence has to be renewed, at that time through the tourism ministry. We could not confirm from an official page which office issues and renews it today, and the sources we found disagree, so we do not name one. Ask to see the original licence and check the name, the licence number and the expiry date. Your agency also enters the guide's details when it applies for your TIMS card.
